reports.text: Portable AP chest. Indication: hemoptysis. Heart size normal. Patchy airspace opacities in both lungs. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: ICU Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medical ICU
Nephrology consultation, 04/01/2026
Requested by: ICU team, for hemoptysis with abnormal urine.

HPI: 34-year-old man with ADPKD, CKD stage 1 and hypertension, known to our outpatient group, who was seen originally for headaches and high blood pressure and last summer for a pit viper bite on the leg. He has noticed dark urine for about a week and began coughing up blood two days ago. No fever, chest pain or recent infection.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father ADPKD; paternal uncle ruptured cerebral aneurysm; mother HTN.
Social: accountant. Never smoker. Former social drinker, none in over a year.

Exam: T 36.8 C, BP 142/88, HR 80, RR 16, SpO2 92% on room air, now on 2 L nasal cannula. Speaking full sentences. Crackles scattered through both lung fields. Heart regular. Abdomen with large palpable kidneys bilaterally, nontender. No edema, no rash.

Data: creatinine 2.4 (normal at our office in December), BUN 38. Hemoglobin 11.6. UA: large blood, protein 1+, many RBCs with dysmorphic forms on microscopy. Chest film: patchy bilateral infiltrates.

Assessment: pulmonary-renal syndrome; leading concern anti-GBM disease (Goodpasture syndrome), with ANCA vasculitis the main alternative.

Recommendations:
- Send anti-GBM antibody, MPO and PR3 ANCA.
- Do not wait for serology: methylprednisolone 500 mg IV daily x3 starting today.
- Temporary right internal jugular catheter and daily plasma exchange to begin today.
- Hold lisinopril.
- Kidney biopsy would usually be done, but with enlarged polycystic kidneys the bleeding risk is high; we will rely on serology if strongly positive.
- We will follow daily.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital
Admitted 04/01/2026 (ICU 04/01-04/05, then medical floor). Discharged 04/16/2026.

Principal diagnosis: anti-glomerular basement membrane disease (Goodpasture syndrome) with alveolar hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis.
Other: ADPKD, hypertension.

Course: Presented with a week of dark urine and two days of hemoptysis; SpO2 92% on room air, crackles bilaterally, patchy bilateral infiltrates on chest film, creatinine 2.4, active urinary sediment. Admitted to the ICU. Anti-GBM antibody returned at 186 U/mL (reference <20); MPO and PR3 ANCA negative. Biopsy deferred given polycystic kidneys; diagnosis made on serology with the clinical picture.

Treatment: methylprednisolone 500 mg IV daily x3, then prednisone 60 mg daily. Plasma exchange daily via a right IJ temporary catheter, 14 sessions in total; catheter removed 04/15 without complication. Oral cyclophosphamide 100 mg daily started (dose reduced for kidney function), planned for 3 months. PJP prophylaxis and a PPI added. Lisinopril held.

Respiratory: 2 L nasal cannula days 1-3, hemoptysis stopped by day 3, weaned to room air and transferred out of the ICU on day 4.
Renal: creatinine peaked at 2.7 on day 3 and improved to 1.9 at discharge. Urine output stayed adequate; no dialysis needed.
Heme: hemoglobin 11.6 on arrival, 10.9 at discharge; no transfusion.
Anti-GBM antibody 34 U/mL on 04/15.

Discharge medications:
- prednisone 60 mg by mouth daily (3 x 20 mg)
- cyclophosphamide 100 mg by mouth daily, morning, with plenty of fluids
- sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim 400/80 mg one tablet daily
- pantoprazole 40 mg daily
- HOLD lisinopril until nephrology review
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within one week. Nephrology clinic in 3 weeks. Weekly-to-biweekly CBC and BMP while on cyclophosphamide (standing order sent to PCP's lab). Avoid live vaccines. Return for any hemoptysis, fever, or decreased urine.

documents.title: Nephrology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient nephrology, 05/07/2026.

First clinic visit after admission for anti-GBM disease. Feels steadily better; energy returning. No hemoptysis. Urine clear. Tolerating cyclophosphamide, drinking plenty. Steroid side effects: appetite, restless sleep.

Meds: prednisone 60 mg, cyclophosphamide 100 mg, TMP-SMX SS daily, pantoprazole 40 mg. Lisinopril on hold. NKDA.

Labs 05/05 (drawn at an outside lab): creatinine 1.6; anti-GBM 28 U/mL; CBC with normal WBC and platelets.

Assessment: anti-GBM disease responding; antibody nearly cleared, kidney function improving. ADPKD.
Plan:
- Reduce prednisone to 40 mg daily.
- Continue cyclophosphamide 100 mg (3-month course ends early July), TMP-SMX, pantoprazole.
- Labs every 2 weeks as ordered.
- Chest x-ray, 2 views, to document clearing.
- Return in 4 weeks.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Comparison: portable chest 04/01/2026. The previously seen patchy opacities in both lungs have cleared. Lungs are clear. Heart size and mediastinum normal. No effusion or pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Resolution of prior bilateral infiltrates. Clear lungs.

documents.title: Nephrology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient nephrology, 06/04/2026.

Doing well, back to work part-time from home. No respiratory symptoms. Chest x-ray 05/13 clear.

Labs 06/02: anti-GBM 8 U/mL (negative); creatinine 1.5; hemoglobin 13.4; WBC and platelets normal; urine albumin/creatinine 240 mg/g.

Assessment: anti-GBM disease in serologic remission. Residual albuminuria after glomerular injury, superimposed on ADPKD.
Plan:
- Prednisone down to 20 mg daily.
- Restart lisinopril 10 mg daily for albuminuria and blood pressure; BMP in 2 weeks with the standing labs.
- Finish cyclophosphamide early July as planned.
- Continue TMP-SMX and pantoprazole.
- Return in 4 weeks.
NKDA.

documents.title: Nephrology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient nephrology, 07/02/2026.

Three months from presentation. Asymptomatic. Back to full-time work.

Labs 06/30: creatinine 1.4; potassium normal on lisinopril; WBC and platelets normal throughout the course.

Assessment: anti-GBM disease in remission after plasma exchange, steroids and 3 months of oral cyclophosphamide.
Plan:
- Stop cyclophosphamide today; course complete.
- Prednisone 20 mg for now, plan to reduce next visit.
- Continue TMP-SMX while on 20 mg, pantoprazole, lisinopril 10 mg.
- Labs early August (CBC, BMP, UA, urine albumin/creatinine, anti-GBM), visit after.
NKDA.

documents.title: Nephrology Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient nephrology, 08/06/2026.

Feels well. Lifting again. No hemoptysis, no gross hematuria.

Meds: prednisone 20 mg, TMP-SMX SS, pantoprazole 40 mg, lisinopril 10 mg. Cyclophosphamide completed 07/02. NKDA.

Labs 08/04: creatinine 1.4 (eGFR in the 60s), stable for 5 weeks; UA trace blood; urine albumin/creatinine 150 mg/g, down from 240; anti-GBM negative.

Assessment:
1. Anti-GBM disease, sustained serologic remission. Relapse is uncommon.
2. CKD now stage 2 (new baseline creatinine 1.4) with albuminuria, on a background of ADPKD.
3. Hypertension, controlled on lisinopril.
Plan:
- Prednisone to 10 mg daily.
- Stop TMP-SMX.
- Continue pantoprazole while on prednisone.
- Continue lisinopril 10 mg.
- Labs and visit in 6 weeks.
